themes_detail.label: E-Scooter Surge
themes_detail.summary: E-scooter complaints spiked 700% THIS WEEK to 3 complaints versus a 0.4 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 5.42), suggesting rapid deployment or enforcement of a micro-mobility service in Williamsbridge/Baychester that residents are not yet adapted to.
evidence: 3 e-scooter complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 average weekly complaints over prior 8 weeks
700% spike represents statistically significant anomaly (z-score: 5.42, severity: high)
Spike is the most recent emerging signal in dataset (this week)
reporting_angles: Did a new e-scooter company launch service in CD 212 this week? Interview the operator and residents about safety concerns.
What are the specific complaints? Unsafe parking, riding behavior, or infrastructure conflicts?

themes_detail.label: Vehicle Noise Escalation
themes_detail.summary: Vehicle noise complaints surged 241% LAST WEEK to 29 complaints versus an 8.5 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.8), indicating a sharp uptick in loud cars, motorcycles, or commercial vehicles disturbing the neighborhood.
evidence: 29 vehicle noise complaints filed LAST WEEK vs. 8.5 average weekly complaints over prior 8 weeks
241% spike represents statistically significant anomaly (z-score: 4.8, severity: high)
Signal appeared within last 2 weeks, making it highly current
reporting_angles: Interview residents about timing, location, and character of noise (motorcycle clubs, street racing, commercial delivery trucks). Is it concentrated in one area?
Has NYPD increased patrols or enforcement? Check precinct data on noise summonses and vehicle violations.

themes_detail.label: Graffiti Spike Two Weeks Ago
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints jumped 392% TWO WEEKS AGO to 8 complaints versus a 1.6 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 5.23), suggesting either a coordinated tagging incident or delayed cleanup, though the signal may be subsiding.
evidence: 8 graffiti complaints filed 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 1.6 average weekly complaints over prior 8 weeks
392% spike represents statistically significant anomaly (z-score: 5.23, severity: high)
Spike occurred 2 weeks ago; current status of complaints this week is unclear, making this a secondary lead
reporting_angles: Was this a single graffiti incident or coordinated tagging? Map complaint locations to identify hot spots.
What is the current status of cleanup? Follow up with Parks Department on remediation timeline.

themes_detail.label: Illegal Parking Uptick
themes_detail.summary: Illegal parking complaints rose 32% LAST WEEK to 270 complaints versus a 204.0 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.17), indicating sustained parking pressure in a neighborhood already burdened by 2,790 complaints over 90 days—the third-highest complaint category.
evidence: 270 illegal parking complaints filed LAST WEEK vs. 204.0 average weekly complaints over prior 8 weeks
32% spike represents statistically significant anomaly (z-score: 4.17, severity: high)
Illegal parking is third-highest complaint volume overall (2,790 over 90 days), indicating chronic problem with acute worsening
reporting_angles: What is driving the recent uptick? New development activity, reduced enforcement, or seasonal factors?
Interview residents about how illegal parking affects daily life and whether street design changes could help (better signage, enforcement cameras).

themes_detail.label: Plumbing Complaints Collapse
themes_detail.summary: Plumbing complaints dropped 85% THIS WEEK to 8 complaints versus a 51.9 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: -5.44), representing an unusual and statistically significant decline that warrants investigation into whether data reporting, processing, or response patterns have changed.
evidence: 8 plumbing complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 51.9 average weekly complaints over prior 8 weeks
85% decline represents statistically significant anomaly (z-score: -5.44, severity: high)
Plumbing is 7th-highest complaint category overall (631 over 90 days), so sudden disappearance is noteworthy
reporting_angles: Is this a data reporting issue or genuine decline? Verify with 311 system and DOB whether complaints are being categorized differently.
If genuine: Did a large-scale plumbing repair initiative launch? Check DOB permits and HPD enforcement actions.
